================================================================================
 BioShock Remastered VR  |  1.0.3
================================================================================

The hands release. Both of your hands are now in the game, weapons hold still
enough to actually aim down, and the scripted moments finally put you where they
meant to. Underneath all of that, the whole codebase was rebuilt so the next
release does not take as long as this one did.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 HIGHLIGHTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

YOUR OTHER HAND EXISTS NOW
  The hand that is not holding your weapon used to be hidden. It appears, it
  follows your controller, and it turns with it, whether you are holding a
  weapon or a plasmid. On the two-handed guns you can also reach across and take
  hold of the barrel: grip where the game already draws its own hand on the
  fore-end and the weapon points along both of your hands. Recoil no longer
  shakes you loose from it.

THE GUN HOLDS STILL, SO IT CAN BE AIMED
  The game animates the arm your weapon hangs off, so the gun drifted and
  breathed in your hand. That made a calibrated crosshair impossible and iron
  sights pointless. The animation is now frozen while you hold a weapon. Every
  weapon takes its own grip, angle and crosshair, tunable live in the headset on
  the numpad and saved to your ini as you go. The crossbow, grenade launcher and
  chemical thrower shipped untuned before. They are tuned now.

SCRIPTED SCENES GO WHERE THEY ARE SUPPOSED TO
  Where a scene walked you used to depend on which way you happened to be
  looking or pointing when it triggered, and the balcony fall could land you
  several metres from where it intended. Scenes now land correctly and frame
  themselves correctly no matter where you were aiming. You can still turn with
  the right stick during one, and the scene reclaims its framing as it rotates.
  Your arms and hands appear only while the game is genuinely animating them,
  instead of hanging frozen in your view.

THE INTERFACE STAYS IN THE ROOM
  The map, the manual, the upgrade machine, the Gene Bank and the whole
  plasmid and tonic flow are placed in the world instead of riding your head.
  That includes clicking through from one page of a machine screen to the next,
  which is what broke most of them before. The world holds still behind a screen
  while you read it.

PER-PLASMID TUNING
  Every plasmid shared one set of numbers, so tuning Electro Bolt moved
  Telekinesis with it. Each plasmid keeps its own position, angle and crosshair
  now, and switching between them restores what you set.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 ADDED
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * A real tracked second hand, with a weapon or a plasmid
  * Two-handed grip on the weapons that support it
  * Four movement modes. What steers your walking is now separate from what aims
    your weapon, so any combination of the two works
  * Snap turn, with an adjustable step
  * Haptic feedback on firing, on the grab zone, and on the actions that earn it
  * Live in-headset tuning for weapon position, angle, crosshair, off-hand
    position and off-hand angle, saved automatically per weapon
  * Manual weapon swing (early, and it will get better)
  * Per-plasmid grip and crosshair calibration
  * Setup asks which headset and which runtime you have and configures the
    controls to match, including moving the d-pad modifier off the thumb rest on
    trackpad controllers, where it silently stopped you walking
  * Uninstall script, which restores your game config and keeps your tuning
  * One-click log collector for bug reports
  * Interaction profiles for Index, Vive and WMR controllers
  * Around 130 settings in the ini, all documented in it

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 CHANGED
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * Locomotion and aiming are completely decoupled
  * Weapon sway disabled, so iron sights are usable
  * Crosshair logic rebuilt to be consistent, and it hides itself when your
    hands are empty or a scene is playing
  * Native OpenXR is now the default runtime. The SteamVR shim is the fallback
    for headsets with no 32-bit OpenXR runtime
  * Turn speed no longer changes with how hard you push. The game's own response
    curve is nearly vertical at the top of the stick, which was the whole of
    "sometimes slow, sometimes fast"
  * Better default ini settings for comfort and compatibility
  * Improved Epic support, verified against a real Epic install
  * Better performance, and better logging and error reporting throughout
  * Whole codebase refactored. No behaviour change, much faster changes ahead

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 FIXED
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * The gene machines and Gatherer's Gardens now place their text correctly
  * Walking in a straight line while pointing elsewhere drifted your path by up
    to 11 degrees, and collapsed to a pure sidestep near 90
  * Loading screens ran at half framerate
  * Health and plasmid HUD meters
  * Cutscene black bars
  * Screen shake and injected camera rotation during normal play
  * The crosshair showing with nothing in your hands
  * Quest arrow position and scale
  * Rotational slew when entering a scripted event
  * Inconsistent turn speed
  * The pause and radial menus submitting both eyes, which juddered the world
    behind them
  * The desktop mirror submitting both eyes
  * The grab point wandering mid-fight, and the weapon slipping out of your off
    hand between shots
  * A constant rumble in the left hand from the game's idle animation
  * Multiple bugs in the controller binding configs
  * An installer that could report success after failing
  * The mod loader needed a Visual C++ redistributable that many machines do not
    have. When it was missing, nothing loaded and no log was written to say why

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 KNOWN ISSUES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * Pre-rendered cutscenes that play during the game are not anchored to the
    room yet, so they still follow your head
  * Walking through water draws its effect as a square rather than filling your
    view
  * The quest arrow drifts with the weapon before settling back
  * Your arms sit slightly low and forward in some scripted scenes
  * The desktop mirror runs at about half the headset's framerate. That is how
    the game submits frames to its own window, not a performance problem. For
    recording, use SteamVR's display view
  * dxgi.dll is also how ReShade, Special K and DXVK load, and only one thing
    can own that filename, so they cannot be used together yet
  * SteamVR performance can degrade after about 30 minutes with Virtual Desktop
    on Meta headsets. This is a Meta driver issue rather than something the mod
    can fix. VirtualDesktopSwitcher resolves it for some people:
    https://github.com/webhead2oo9/VirtualDesktopSwitcher
  * Most of the polish work happened in the early game. The systems are built to
    be general, but I have not seen every feature in every part of the game
  * Only Meta Touch controllers are tested. Index, Vive and WMR bindings are
    built from each device's published layout, but I do not own that hardware.
    Reports are very welcome either way


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 CREDITS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Built on the Khronos OpenXR SDK and MinHook.

A huge thank you to Eye-will, who playtested every new build and gave me
consistently sharp, genuinely useful feedback. A lot of what got fixed this
release got fixed because they took the time to describe exactly what they saw.

And to VOID, developer of github.com/mohamad-balouza/bioshock-vr, for his
massive contributions to this project. His work is MIT licensed and he gave me
explicit permission to use it however this mod needed. Several of the hardest
parts here exist because of that:

  * Disabling the game's flat 2D reticle through the engine's own console path,
    which is what let a proper VR crosshair replace it
  * The hand rig's bone map: which bones are the wrists, which five per side are
    forearm, and which one the weapon hangs off. That is what makes it possible
    to hide the arms without losing the gun
  * Capturing the whole interface in one render target pass, which is how the
    HUD gets lifted onto its own panel
  * The animation-preserving skeletal drive, which is the idea behind freezing
    the weapon hand. That is what killed weapon sway and made aiming calibratable
  * Reading the barrel direction from the model's own bones rather than guessing
    at it with a tuned constant
  * Locating the engine function that decides where a shot starts and which way
    it goes, and the technique for substituting our own values into it

His research is public, and it saved me weeks. Every system above came from
there, and this list gets a new line every time another one does.
